issues: Summary says the brothers are urged to be faithful, but omits the quoted appeal to go up again; this is a minor incompleteness.
Nephi addresses his brethren; only scene 2 explicitly identifies Laman, Lemuel, and Sam among them, so identifying this group as those named brothers here is contextual inference.

Summary changes the chronology: verse 5 places the brothers hiding outside the walls before Nephi enters the city, but says they remain hidden as Nephi moves through the city toward Laban’s house; verse 6 reports his being led by the Spirit, not a spoken statement.
The inference that Nephi approaches Laban is reasonable from “when I came to him,” but the exact action is not otherwise specified.
The verse reports Nephi’s inward thoughts and shrinking; depicting him visibly hesitating with the sword near Laban is a reasonable but unspecified visual interpretation.

The quoted line attributed to the Spirit from verse 13 is not verbatim: the source begins “Behold the Lord slayeth the wicked to bring forth his righteous purposes.” The supplied dialogue changes this into a different sentence.
The verse 14 excerpt is a contiguous exact quotation but begins mid-sentence; as narration it may misleadingly present only a fragment of the remembered conditional promise.
“Holds or carries the treasury keys” is not established; the verse says the servant had the keys, without specifying how they are held.

The verse 24 dialogue excerpt is exact, but the verse 25 excerpt “that he should follow me” is narration rendered as a fragment of Nephi’s speech; the source says Nephi bade him to follow, without supplying those words as direct dialogue.
The selected verse 32 dialogue fragment is exact but omits the verse’s conditional and oath context, which could make the offer sound unconditional.
